slides.lead: It's legal: one type of bottled water can come from any source, including public supplies.

paras: In England, bottled water is sold as one of three types.
slides.source: DEFRA, COMPARE TYPES OF BOTTLED WATER

paras: From a protected underground source, bottled at the spring or borehole.
No disinfection. Only five treatments are allowed, and its composition must go on the label.

items.l: YEARS IT CAN TAKE TO BE RECOGNISED

slides.lead: The local authority must recognise it before it can be sold.

paras: Spring water: underground, bottled at the source, any treatment allowed.
Bottled drinking water: any source, including public supplies. Any treatment, not listed on the label.
Bottled water is regulated by local authorities.
Tap water in England is overseen by the Drinking Water Inspectorate.
Public water supplies in England met the standards in 99.97% of tests in 2025.

tips: 'Natural mineral water': recognised source, no disinfection.
'Bottled drinking water': could come from any source.
cta: Comment which you drink, and your town.
